To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we designed and tested gapmer AON with or without a LNA modification to knock-down a pathogenic mutation causing autosomal dominant Retinitis Pigementosa (adRP).

we have designed antisense oligonucletides to silence a dominant-negative pathogenic variant of NR2E3 and have demonstrated that the AONs are able to reduce the levels of both the mutant and wild type allele, indicating that further modifications are necessary to increase allele-specific targeting.

we show the first proof-of-principle for AON-mediated allele-specific knockdown of a single nucleotid variation causing a dominant negative effect, as a therapeutic approach in a model of autosomal dominant retinal disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a proof-of-concept of antisense oligonucelotide (AON)-mediated silencing of a pathogenic variant in Nuclear Receptors 2E3 (NR2e3) associated autosomal dominant retinal disease.

the design of a novel antisense oligonucelotide for a single nucleotide mutation with dominant negative effect in the NR2E3 gene, which underlies 1–2% of autosomal dominant retinal dystrophies (adRD).
the development of antisense oligonucletide (AON)-mediated knockdown of the G56 variant causing NR2E3-related adRP.
